findings.summary: The page titled and subtitled as the registries chapter contains almost entirely security and resource-limit material, so the registry topic is never actually taught.
findings.evidence: page_title "Registries: Push, Pull and Tag Strategy", subtitle "(Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR and self-hosted)", but the blocks are a `--memory 512m` / `--cpus 1` / `--pids-limit 100` cap table, "Deny by default" (`--cap-drop=ALL --read-only --user app`), "5. Common Mistakes" ("Mounting `/var/run/docker.sock`: that container **owns** the host"), a "Blast Radius of One App Bug" diagram, and a second near-identical cap table; the only registry content is the last four-line code block "docker login reg / docker tag local reg/org/img:1.0 / docker push ...".
findings.fix: Move every security/limits block on page 1 to page 2 (where it belongs under "Security and Resource Limits") and rebuild page 1 from the registry syllabus points: registry vs repository definition, Hub as default plus GHCR/ECR/ACR, official vs verified vs community images, `docker login` credential storage, the tag→push→pull flow, tagging strategy (semver + major + git SHA), digest pinning, Hub rate limits, self-hosted `registry:2`, and scanning/signing.

findings.summary: Page 1's title and subtitle promise a registry lesson, but almost the entire page is security and resource-limit material.
findings.evidence: page_title "Registries: Push, Pull and Tag Strategy" / subtitle "(Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR and self-hosted)" sits above a `--memory 512m` / `--cpus 1` / `--pids-limit 100` cap table, a "Deny by default" callout ("Start from `--cap-drop=ALL --read-only --user app`"), a "5. Common Mistakes" list about `/var/run/docker.sock`, a "Blast Radius of One App Bug" diagram and a second flags-vs-guards table; only the final code block (`docker login` / `tag` / `push` / `pull ...@sha256`) is about registries.
findings.fix: Retitle page 1 to match its body, e.g. "Least Privilege and Hard Resource Caps" with subtitle "(cap-drop, read-only, memory, CPU, pids, logs)", and move the registry title onto a page whose blocks actually cover push/pull/tag strategy.

findings.summary: BuildKit's `--mount=type=secret` is listed as a runtime secret-injection mechanism, but it is build-time only and does nothing for a running container.
findings.evidence: "Inject at runtime: secret store env, Docker secrets, or BuildKit `--mount=type=secret`"
findings.fix: Split the bullet: runtime = secret-store env vars, Docker/Compose secrets mounted as files; build-time = BuildKit `RUN --mount=type=secret` (keeps the secret out of layers and `docker history`).

findings.summary: The security page begins at section 3 and never presents sections 1–2 for its own topic, so least privilege and secrets — promised in its subtitle — are asserted nowhere on the page that owns them.

findings.fix: Bring the least-privilege and secrets blocks back from page 1 as sections "1. Definition: least privilege" and "2. Secrets", then let sections 3–5 follow.

findings.summary: The "lean, cache-friendly build" Dockerfile never sets a WORKDIR, so `/app` is never created and the final-stage `COPY --from=build /app /app` fails the build.
findings.evidence: ["FROM node:22-slim AS build","COPY package*.json ./","RUN npm ci && npm cache clean -f","COPY . .","FROM node:22-slim","COPY --from=build /app /app"] with note "deps before source; slim final stage"
findings.fix: Add `WORKDIR /app` immediately after `FROM node:22-slim AS build` (and in the final stage), so the copied manifests, sources and `node_modules` actually live at `/app` and `COPY --from=build /app /app` resolves.

findings.summary: The table presents `--memory-swap 512m` as a swap cap, but the flag sets the combined memory+swap total and is rejected when used without `--memory`.
findings.evidence: ["Swap","`--memory-swap 512m`","silent swap thrash"]
findings.fix: Show the pair and state the semantics: `--memory 512m --memory-swap 512m` = total memory+swap limit; equal values mean swap is disabled.

findings.summary: The multi-line `docker run` resource-limit snippet is not a valid command: the `--memory-swap` line ends in a comment with no line continuation, so the command is cut in two.
findings.evidence: ["docker run --memory 512m \\","  --memory-swap 512m   # no swap","  --cpus 1 --pids-limit 100 \\", ...]
findings.fix: Move the inline comment off the continued line (e.g. put `# same value = swap disabled` above the command, or use `--memory-swap 512m \`), so every line except the last ends with a backslash and the image name `app` terminates one command.
